item.title: OpenQodex adds pre-push code review for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor
item.description:
OpenQodex adds pre-push code review for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor

Open source code review tool OpenQodex now runs inside coding agents to check every change before you push. It operates without requiring a separate account or API key, acting as a separate reviewer that validates code changes made by agents in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenQodex is an open source code review tool for coding agents.
  • It runs a separate reviewer that checks every change an agent writes before the user pushes.
  • No account or key of its own is required.
  • It is available for use in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline.

🧩 How it works

  • Code Graph: A code graph provides the agent with a map of the codebase.
  • Scanner Integration: It runs scanners that fit the changed files, keeping findings on the changed lines. A scanner is a program that checks code without a model, such as gitleaks or semgrep.
  • Dependency Check: Every supported lockfile in the repository is checked against osv.dev at every review and scan of a change. Advisories outside the changed lines are shown but never counted.
  • Fresh Reviewers: Separate Claude Code or Codex processes on the user’s login run the review, with no memory of the current session.
  • Verification: A script checks every line a reviewer quotes as evidence against the code. Verifiers confirm or refute every candidate and every scanner finding.

⚙️ Key details

  • Initiation: Users say to their agent, “review my change with openqodex”.
  • Setup: The init command finds agents on the machine, lists the files it will write, and asks for confirmation once.
  • Terminal Execution: In your own terminal, run ~/.openqodex/bin/openqodex review.
  • Sandbox Limitation: In its default sandbox, Codex gives commands no network, so the terminal command must be run outside the sandbox.
  • Scope: The review covers commits not yet pushed plus everything uncommitted.
  • Output: The tool prints a receipt with the verdict, one line per finding, and the path to report.html. It also writes report.md, report.json, and report.sarif.

🚀 Availability

  • Works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, and Goose.
  • The host identifier can be claude-code, codex, cursor, cline, or goose.
  • An npx install does not put OpenQodex on the system PATH.
  • The reviewer was tested with Claude Code 2.1.330 using claude-opus-5-5.

#OpenQodex #CodeReview #AIagents #ClaudeCode #OpenSource

Source: openqodex/openqodex

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to automate code review and approvals
item.description:
Anthropic launches Claude Ship to automate code review and approvals

Anthropic has launched Claude Ship, a new product that enables AI to review, fix, and approve pull requests to help software engineers ship code.

🧩 How it works

Claude Ship introduces two new agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, which are launching in beta. These agents build upon the previously released Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October.

  • PR Steward: Jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members, and leaves comments on what it changed.
  • Claude Approvals: Can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it.

Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Function
PR Steward Addresses failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback
Claude Approvals Approves routine changes based on organizational policy
Decision Inputs Considers Code Review findings or custom classifiers using natural language

🚀 Availability

Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

#Anthropic #Claude #AI #SoftwareEngineering #CodeReview

Source: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now

item.title: Code Review Graph for AI Coding Tools
item.description:
Code Review Graph for AI Coding Tools

🔍 Overview

Code Review Graph is an AI development tool that builds a persistent map of your codebase to give AI coding tools precise review context over MCP.

🧩 How it works

  • Builds a local-first code intelligence graph for MCP and CLI.
  • Creates a local code knowledge graph that gives AI coding tools precise review context over MCP.
  • Uses Tree-sitter to build a structural map of the code and serves compact context over MCP.

⚙️ Key details

  • Requires Python 3.10+.
  • Installs hooks and skills where the tool supports them.
  • Uses a SQLite file for storage.
  • Cloud embeddings are opt-in.

🚀 Availability

  • Available for installation.
  • Can be installed using the install command.

💡 Why it matters

  • Reduces the amount of code that AI coding tools need to read.
  • Improves the accuracy of AI coding tools.
  • Enhances the overall coding experience.

#AIAgents #MachineLearning #CodeReview

Source: tirth8205/code-review-graph

item.title: Hodor: An Agentic LLM‑Powered Code Reviewer for Git Repositories
item.description:
Hodor: An Agentic LLM‑Powered Code Reviewer for Git Repositories

A new AI tool called Hodor provides an agentic code reviewer that can be run on GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests, Gitea/Forgejo pull requests, and local diffs.

🔍 Overview

  • Reviews code changes by invoking an LLM agent with confined inspection tools (git_diff, read, grep, find, ls).
  • Returns structured findings as inline comments and a summary note, or prints them locally.
  • Supports a default review protocol that remains unchanged unless explicitly overridden.

🧩 How it works

  1. Hodor checks out the change and automatically resolves to the git repository root, even when invoked from a subdirectory.
  2. It supplies the LLM with the limited toolset listed above and asks for a structured review.
  3. Findings are posted as inline comments and a summary, or output to the console.
  4. Optional instruction files can be added; they are additive, repeatable, and later files win conflicts, while --focus instructions win over file‑based instructions.
  5. The --profile security flag prefixes the bundled security‑review instructions before any explicit instruction files, narrowing reporting to security vulnerabilities without replacing the baseline protocol.

⚙️ Key details

  • Included changes: uncommitted (staged + unstaged) changes, not only committed code.
  • Repository handling: skips PR metadata fetching and workspace cloning.
  • Default model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.
  • Reasoning effort: Adaptive.
  • Optional flags:
    • --ultrathink – Off
    • --full – Off
    • --post – disabled (no remote posting)
    • --target-branch – None
  • Supported LLM providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, OpenRouter; other providers are best‑effort.
Flag / Option Default / State Description
--model anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 Base LLM used for the review
--reasoning-effort Adaptive Level of reasoning effort applied
--ultrathink Off Extended reasoning mode (disabled)
--full Off Full‑snapshot review mode (disabled)
--post Disabled Remote posting of comments (disabled)
--target-branch None Branch to compare against (none by default)

🚀 Availability

  • Docker images are published at ghcr.io/mr-karan/hodor:<version> for use in CI pipelines.
  • Pinning a version in CI keeps reviews comparable across runs.
  • When installed globally via npm install -g, the command npx @mrkaran/hodor can be replaced with hodor.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables consistent, automated code reviews across multiple Git platforms without requiring repository cloning.
  • Allows security‑focused reviews via --profile security or --focus "Report only security findings." while preserving baseline defect checks.
  • Supports a range of LLM back‑ends, making it adaptable to existing infrastructure.
  • Works on local, uncommitted changes, helping developers catch issues before committing.

#AI #CodeReview #DevOps #LLM

Source: mr-karan/hodor

item.title: Claude introduces continuous AI‑assisted code review
item.description:
Claude introduces continuous AI‑assisted code review

Claude Haiku 5.5 brings continuous AI‑assisted code review to the Claude Code team.

🔍 Overview

We think “did a human read the code?” is an imprecise proxy for “what could go wrong with this change, and which check—automated or human—is the right one to catch it?” — Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang, How the Claude Code team does code review

  • “Before, review was a gate at the end of the road: write the code, open a PR, wait for your colleague.”
  • “Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write.”
  • “Asking that question also changed when review happens.”

🧩 How it works

  • “Most changes have been reviewed and fixed by Claude at least once before a human is asked to look.”
  • The system decides which check—automated or human—is the right one to catch potential problems.

💡 Why it matters

  • “This catches most routine mistakes, and saves team attention for higher‑level questions and scrutiny.”

🚀 Availability

  • Claude Haiku 5.5 – 7th October 2026

#Claude #CodeReview #AI

Source: A quote from Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt, and Qing Wang
